headline: Shifting Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill aims to make large energy users, such as data centers, responsible for their own grid infrastructure costs, potentially reducing the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger, U.S. Sen. Mark Warner, consumer advocacy organizations, utility watchdog organizations.
opponents: Data center industry (implied, as they would bear increased costs).
news_headline: Governor Signs Bills Shifting Data Center Energy Costs
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation directing regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers, ensuring residential customers are not unfairly burdened. This move aims to make data centers pay their fair share for energy generation and distribution.

headline: Mandatory Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires data centers to report their water consumption, aiming to increase transparency and potentially encourage more efficient water use.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Potomac Conservancy, environmental and water advocates.
opponents: Data center industry (implied, as they are being "singled out" and have concerns about reporting).
news_headline: New Virginia Law Mandates Data Center Water Reporting
news_summary: A new Virginia law, SB 553, requires local water authorities to publicly report data center water usage. Sponsored by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, the law aims to increase transparency regarding the industry's water consumption.

headline: Local Control Over Data Center Siting
short_summary: This bill grants local governments more authority to regulate the siting and noise levels of data centers, addressing community concerns.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local governments, residents concerned about noise and environmental impact.
opponents: Data center industry (implied, as they face new regulations and assessments).
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Address Data Center Siting and Noise
news_summary: HB 153 requires site assessments for new data centers to examine sound profiles near residential areas and schools. It also allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites, giving local governments more regulatory power.
